messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: VentureX fleet footprint & token-sample request

Samir —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To get a clean dedicated sizing estimate we need a very small sample of real traffic and a few clarifications. Can you confirm the items below and drop the sample CSV when you can? A quick response will let us turn around a reserved-capacity sketch by EOD next week.

1) Token/sample data: a CSV with 200 representative requests (prompt tokens, response tokens, model used per request) helps us estimate KV cache hit behavior and typical sequence lengths. Something like: id,prompt_tokens,response_tokens,model,label
2) Concurrency targets: steady QPS and desired P95 latency target for interactive endpoints (ms), and any background batch/async jobs (throughput-target/minute).
3) Session behavior: average session length (messages per conversation), fraction of sessions that are multi-turn (>3 messages).
4) Dayparting/seasonality: any daily/hourly peaks, weekdays vs weekend differences, and an expected peak multiplier.
5) SLA tolerance: acceptable fallback path (lower-capacity variant) and percentage of traffic that can be degraded if capacity constrained.

Attachments: please attach the CSV and any traffic heatmaps. If you prefer, we can accept an anonymized sample.

Next steps from our side: Marissa will map the sample to GPU SKUs and Vivek will propose autoscaling guardrails.

Best,
Ben

Ben —

Thanks, attaching an anonymized CSV (venturex_token_sample_q2.csv) and a weekly heatmap (weekly_traffic_heatmap.png). Quick notes below:

- Sample covers our customer-facing chat (product-recommendations) for the last two weeks. Column layout matches your example (id,prompt_tokens,response_tokens,model,label).
- Steady-state: ~18 qps across our US region; peak windows hit ~120 qps for ~10 minutes (daily), typically between 12:30-12:40 PST.
- Latency target: P95 <= 280ms for interactive endpoints. We can accept up to 10% degraded traffic during extreme peak.
- Session behavior: avg 4 messages/session, ~35% multi-turn (>3). Background batch jobs: a nightly summarization pipeline that sends ~6k requests over 30 minutes (can be scheduled).

Aisha (cc) is our platform lead — she can share historical retention numbers if useful.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | VentureX
samir@venturex.ai

Samir — great, thanks for the files. Quick clarifying questions after a skim:

- For the 120 qps peaks, is that sustained across multiple frontends (i.e., global fan-out) or concentrated in a single region? You said US region — is that us-west-only?
- The nightly summarization: what model variant does it use (smaller quantized model vs production gpt-like variant)? That changes how we recommend spot/batch capacity.
- P95 target 280ms — is that network-to-client or server-generation only? We typically size for generation time, excluding transit.

If we get confirmation on the above, Marissa will send a preliminary GPU mapping (sku mix) and Vivek will propose an autoscale+burst policy that keeps your cost predictable while meeting the P95.

Ben

Subject: RE: VentureX fleet footprint & token-sample request

Looping in a quick mapping proposal based on the sample:

- Interactive tier (P95 280ms): recommend reserving a baseline pool of 8xA100-80GB equivalent GPUs with autoscale to +3 nodes for sustained bursts; this handles ~22 qps steady per node with KV cache and quantized 16-bit kernels. For the 120 qps 10-minute daily spikes, enable burst policy to route to preemptible nodes (if tolerated) or fall back to a smaller model for ~20% of sessions.
- Batch/nightly summarization: schedule into a sized low-priority pool (2xRTX6000-equivalent) and run with a 2-hour window to avoid interfering with interactive SLAs.
- Expected token egress/cost: based on the sample CSV, projected 330M tokens/month across the fleet — we'll attach a cost delta in the full proposal.

Ben/Vivek — I attached a draft reserved_capacity_proposal_v0.2.pdf (stub) to illustrate the SKU mapping and suggested rollout (can convert to a commitment/RFO).

Marissa

Marissa/Ben —

Thanks, that mapping looks reasonable. A couple of quick confirmations:

- The 120 qps peak is concentrated in us-west-2; we can optionally route other regions but primary pressure is west.
- Nightly summarization uses a smaller, quantized variant (qtd-small) — we can schedule to any off-peak window.
- We'd prefer to avoid preemptible nodes for the interactive tier. Please update the proposal to show a pure reserved baseline + a small dedicated burst pool (non-preemptible).

If that version looks good, I can get the procurement team to sign a Statement of Work. Sharing a DocuSign stub we prefer (link below).

Next steps: Ben — can you and Marissa update the PDF to remove preemptible burst and include a short cost delta for non-preemptible burst nodes? If yes, we'll have procurement review this week.

Thanks —
